html:
The conversion of the Nubian kingdom of Nobadia, on the Nile just south of Egypt, to Christianity in 543. Its southern neighbours Makuria and Alodia followed within a few decades.

Nobadia was one of three kingdoms that rose in Nubia after the fall of Kush. The Eastern Roman emperor Justinian and his wife Theodora took opposite sides in the church quarrels of the day over the nature of Christ. According to a church historian, each sent a mission to Nobadia. Theodora's priest, Julian, arrived first, as she had arranged, and the king accepted baptism in her preferred form of the faith.

Makuria converted around 570 and Alodia around 580. Nobadia was later absorbed into Makuria. Churches and cathedrals were built along the Nile, and painted with murals that survive from Faras.

The new Christian kingdoms proved strong. When Arab armies invaded from Egypt in the 640s and 650s, Makuria's archers held them off, and the two sides agreed a treaty of trade and peace. The kingdoms of Christian Nubia lasted until the end of the Middle Ages.
sum: The conversion of the Nubian kingdom of Nobadia, on the Nile just south of Egypt, to Christianity in 543. Its southern neighbours Makuria and Alodia followed within a few decades.
